entries.description: A man in stripped garrison winter gear is standing in the camera's blind spot. He holds a child who is coughing a wet, rattling cough. He pushes a sealed, mil-spec particulate filter into the view of the lens. He does not ask for sanctuary. He asks for a five-day lease on a warm corner.

choices.text: Open the outer door. The child needs the medicine more than the bunker needs the space.
choices.outcomeDescription: He leaves the filter crate in the airlock without being asked. By morning, he has found a mop and started cleaning the intake corridor.

choices.text: Push four ration blocks through the transfer slot. The inner door stays shut.
choices.outcomeDescription: He takes the blocks, leaves the filter, and zips the child into his coat. He walks back into the ash fall without looking at the camera again.

choices.text: Cycle the airlock while aiming through the port. Confiscate the filter.
choices.outcomeDescription: He drops the crate when the bolt racks. He does not curse. He just picks up the child and walks away, which is worse.

entries.description: A woman in heavy, dye-stained wool is standing in front of the camera. The wool is dyed the specific grey of the Ash Sign. She has thrown a satchel of heavy-metal slurry at the base of the door, out of her reach. She holds up both hands. They are cracked with cold.

choices.text: Cycle her into the airlock. Have the dosimeter ready, and burn the grey coat before she enters.
choices.outcomeDescription: She strips out of the coat without argument. By the third day, she is changing bandages in the infirmary, using less iodine than anyone else.

choices.text: Leave the door sealed. Anyone wearing that grey knows what it costs to take it off.
choices.outcomeDescription: The knocking continues for twenty minutes, perfectly rhythmic. Then it stops. At dusk, the sound of a vehicle engine approaches, idles, and leaves.

entries.description: A man wearing Rebuilder yellow over a heavy parka holds a steel thermos up to the camera. His face is wind-burned raw. He taps the side of the thermos, points to a thermometer dial taped to the side, and holds up six fingers. Six hours of battery charge for the heating coil, or the rootstock inside dies.

choices.text: Run a charging cable out through the transfer slot. Keep the door closed.
choices.outcomeDescription: He sits against the concrete for six hours watching the dial. When he unplugs, he leaves a sealed packet of heirloom carrot seeds on the sill.

choices.text: Cycle the airlock. Take the thermos. The roots belong to the bunker now.
choices.outcomeDescription: He does not fight, but he looks at the camera as he backs out of the airlock. Rebuilder caravans bypass your sector for the next three months.

entries.description: Three men in heavy, patched hydrostatic suits have clamped a meter to the exterior intake pipe. One of them holds a clipboard wrapped in plastic. He taps the clipboard against the camera lens. He is demanding thirty liters of clean water as a 'municipal extraction tithe' on behalf of the Hydro Barons. The men behind him are carrying heavy pipe-wrenches and a portable pump.

choices.text: Connect the interior hose to the transfer valve. Run thirty liters into their tank.
choices.outcomeDescription: They watch the pressure gauge closely. When it hits thirty, they shut the valve, stamp a brass tag with a date code, and wire it to your intake pipe.

choices.text: Cut the intercom. Let them try to turn a wrench on reinforced concrete.
choices.outcomeDescription: The man with the clipboard marks a red 'X' over your bunker's grid coordinate. The next day, your exterior water pressure drops to a muddy trickle.

entries.description: Someone in matte-black composite armor is kneeling by the exterior comm port. They do not look at the camera. They slot a heavy military-grade decryption drive into the terminal housing and tap a rhythm on the glass. The screen inside the bunker wakes up, demanding a data dump of all medical and psychological evaluations from the last ninety days.

choices.text: Initiate the transfer. You have no way of stopping the decryption anyway.
choices.outcomeDescription: The transfer bar fills. The figure unplugs the drive, slides a sealed metal box of combat stimulants into the transfer slot, and walks back into the ash fall.

choices.text: Sever the physical hardline to the exterior port from inside the control room.
choices.outcomeDescription: The screen goes dead. The figure stands up, slowly looks directly into the camera lens, and paints a fluorescent tracking mark on the steel door.

entries.description: A woman is leaning heavily against the outer concrete. She is carrying a heavy, lead-lined medical crate, but her gloves are too thin for the weather. She speaks into the intercom, her voice perfectly calm and devoid of panic. She states she is a surgeon, she is developing necrosis in two fingers, and she needs forty-eight hours of ambient heat.

choices.text: Cycle the airlock. Give her a cot near the radiator and two cans of soup.
choices.outcomeDescription: She sleeps for fourteen hours. When she wakes, she spends the next day systematically re-setting every poorly healed bone in the shelter before leaving.

choices.text: Tell her the airlock is broken. It is a lie, but it is easier than saying no.
choices.outcomeDescription: She does not argue. She just picks up the heavy lead crate and begins walking back toward the frozen highway. Her frozen scalpel kit is found near the intake duct the following dawn.

entries.description: Five figures in heavy, cracked lead aprons are kneeling in the snow outside the blast door. Four of them have severe radiation cataracts. The fifth, holding a rusted brass bell, rings it once every ten seconds. They are chanting a slow, toneless litany about the cleansing fire, and asking for ten liters of clean water.

choices.text: Push a jerrycan of filtered water through the transfer slot.
choices.outcomeDescription: The man with the bell pours the water over the snow, blesses the bunker's hinges with a paste of bone-ash and snowmelt, and leads the blind away.

choices.text: Trigger the perimeter warning sirens. Do not open the slot.
choices.outcomeDescription: The sirens are painfully loud. The pilgrims stagger up, disoriented, and wander blindly into a drift of highly radioactive black ash. They do not re-emerge.

entries.description: A man on a battered electric snowmobile stops outside the camera view. He leaves the motor running. He holds up a small, foam-padded case containing a high-frequency quartz resonator. He gestures to the antenna array on your roof, then holds up a hand, opening and closing it three times. Thirty pieces of raw electronic scrap in exchange for hearing the global shortwave broadcasts.

choices.text: Push thirty cleaned circuit boards through the transfer slot.
choices.outcomeDescription: He takes the scrap, leaves the foam case, and drives away. The first thing your radio operator hears is a coastal monitoring station broadcasting weather telemetry in clear, unencrypted English.

choices.text: Ignore him. You already know what is happening in the rest of the world.
choices.outcomeDescription: He waits exactly three minutes, then puts the case back in his coat and accelerates toward the highway. The silence in the comm room feels a little heavier today.

entries.description: Three children, the eldest no more than nine, huddle under the shelter's exterior camera housing. They haven't eaten in four days. They don't knock. They just sit and wait.

choices.text: Open the airlock and bring them inside.
choices.outcomeDescription: They eat slowly and say very little. The eldest keeps watch at the corridor hatch all night, out of habit.

choices.text: Push three days of rations through the supply slot and explain you cannot take them in.
choices.outcomeDescription: They eat where they sit. By morning the camera shows the space empty. The ration wrappers remain.

choices.text: Turn on the exterior floodlight so they can see to move, but do not open the door.
choices.outcomeDescription: The light helps. A survivor who saw them through the periscope stops talking to you for three days.

entries.description: A garrison fire team of four has hammered steel spikes into the concrete forty meters from your intake vent. They are stringing concertina wire. The sergeant reads off a clipboard into a bullhorn: 'You are now within a Territorial Security Zone. Open the outer door for a mandatory structural and biological census. Refusal is an admission of contraband.'

choices.text: Comply with the census. Provide them the sanitized manifest that hides the hydroponics bay.
choices.outcomeDescription: They spend three hours measuring the walls and counting the canned goods. They stamp the manifest, roll up their wire, and move down the highway.

choices.text: Read the pre-war Civilian Defense Code back to him over the intercom.
choices.outcomeDescription: The sergeant stops reading. He makes a slow, deliberate mark on his clipboard, turns his back, and leaves the concertina wire exactly where it is.

choices.text: Roll two charged fuel cells through the transfer slot before he finishes reading.
choices.outcomeDescription: He stops mid-sentence, lowers the bullhorn, and kicks the cells into his rucksack. The checkpoint is dismantled in silence within five minutes.

entries.description: A woman in a thick yellow Rebuilder coat stands by the exterior intake manifold. She is holding a heavy ceramic filtration housing. Over the intercom, she explains she will weld it into your intake line for free. The Rebuilder collective is mapping local groundwater toxicity, and the filter will give them a baseline reading. 'And you get cleaner water,' she adds, wiping frost from her goggles.

choices.text: Cycle her into the intake corridor. Watch her weld the housing.
choices.outcomeDescription: The weld is clean. The water tastes noticeably less like rust. As she packs her tools, you see her log your grid coordinates onto a heavily encrypted tablet.

choices.text: Tell her you don't want the bunker on any maps, even water maps.
choices.outcomeDescription: She nods once, clearly used to this answer. She puts the ceramic housing back in her pack and walks toward the next ridgeline without arguing.

entries.description: A scavenger with severe flash-burn scars on her neck drops a heavy canvas bag in front of the camera. She unrolls it, revealing three functioning analog dosimeters, two sealed gas masks, and an intact Geiger counter with the calibration seal still unbroken. She points to her mouth, then rubs two fingers together. She wants calories or fuel.

choices.text: Push eight ration blocks out for the three dosimeters.
choices.outcomeDescription: She counts the blocks twice. The dosimeters are perfectly calibrated, but the pantry looks noticeably emptier when the door shuts.

choices.text: Offer three vials of antibiotics for the masks and the Geiger counter.
choices.outcomeDescription: She takes the medicine as if it were spun gold. The masks are military-grade, the rubber seals perfectly preserved in talc.

choices.text: Roll out four heavy fuel cells. Take the whole bag.
choices.outcomeDescription: She does not grin, but her shoulders drop two inches. She leaves the entire canvas roll on the sill and walks away faster than she arrived.

entries.description: A Black Ops field handler requests emergency shelter for a compromised deep-cover asset — someone whose cover identity has been burned. The asset is wounded and cannot travel. You are not told their real name.

choices.text: Admit the asset and treat their wounds. No questions.
choices.outcomeDescription: The asset recovers in three days and leaves without speaking to anyone. Handler Voss leaves an encrypted frequency card.

choices.text: Demand full identity disclosure before granting shelter access.
choices.outcomeDescription: Voss stares at you for five seconds, then withdraws without another word.

entries.description: A garrison quartermaster presses a laminated requisition form against the camera glass. The ink is smeared from the cold. He speaks into the intercom in a flat, exhausted voice: 'Emergency fuel reallocation. Sub-section four. Twelve cells.' He adds that a primary garrison heating tanker cracked its jacket in the frost last night.

choices.text: Cycle twelve heavy fuel cells into the transfer airlock.
choices.outcomeDescription: He loads the cells onto a hand-pulled sled. He signs a carbon-copy IOU and drops it in the slot. It's printed on pre-war treasury paper. It might actually be worth something.

choices.text: Recite the 1987 Protection Accords civilian exemption clause.
choices.outcomeDescription: He stares at the speaker grille for a long time. Then he crosses your bunker's coordinates off his clipboard with a heavy black marker and walks away.

choices.text: Push four cells into the airlock. Tell him it's a voluntary donation.
choices.outcomeDescription: He doesn't argue. He loads the four cells, ignores the carbon-copy IOU book, and taps the glass twice in thanks.

entries.description: A man in a heavy rubberized suit is driving steel survey stakes into the permafrost directly above your intake tunnel. He wears the blue armband of the Hydro Barons. When hailed, he says he is mapping the gradient for a new gravity aqueduct. 'If your tunnel intersects the line,' he shouts over the wind, 'we bore right through it. Unless I see blueprints proving otherwise.'

choices.text: Print the original municipal blueprints and drop them out the transfer slot.
choices.outcomeDescription: He photographs the schematics with a bulky field camera, pulls his stakes out of the ground, and moves the survey line fifty meters east.

choices.text: Cycle the exterior automated turret and paint his chest with the laser sight.
choices.outcomeDescription: He does not flinch. He slowly writes a long note on his waterproof clipboard, drops the survey stake exactly where it is, and walks away.

entries.description: Six heavily armed individuals bang the butts of their rifles against the outer blast door. They are wearing a mix of pre-war riot gear and scavenged ballistic plates. They aren't trying to breach; they want attention. Their leader holds up a tactical map to the camera. She shouts that a Hydro Baron column is marching on this sector, and she'll trade the marching orders for three days of safe harbor.

choices.text: Tell them to pass the map through the slot. No one comes inside.
choices.outcomeDescription: She curses, but rolls the map and pushes it through. The intel is highly accurate. They leave to find shelter elsewhere before the Barons arrive.

choices.text: Arm the perimeter turrets. The bunker is closed.
choices.outcomeDescription: The laser sights sweep across their chests. They scatter into the tree line immediately. You never learn what was on the map.

choices.text: Cycle them through the airlock. Confiscate all weapons at the inner door.
choices.outcomeDescription: They surrender fourteen firearms and a bucket of knives. Their map changes your patrol routes permanently, saving at least two lives.

entries.description: An Ash Sign acolyte kneels outside the camera arc. He is wearing a robe woven from shredded Kevlar. When spoken to, he slides a soft clay tablet into the airlock slot. It is damp and smells of river mud. 'For the Ledger of the Living,' he whispers. 'Inscribe your number, that we may count the sparks remaining.'

choices.text: Press the exact population number into the clay with a screwdriver.
choices.outcomeDescription: He receives the tablet with both heavily scarred hands. He bows his head until it touches the steel door, then leaves.

choices.text: Press a fake number into the clay. Half your actual population.
choices.outcomeDescription: He doesn't verify the count. He simply accepts the lie, places it carefully in a leather satchel, and walks away. Your paranoia feels justified.

choices.text: Reject the tablet. You don't participate in cult ledgers.
choices.outcomeDescription: He waits in silence for an hour. Then he draws a circle with a line through it on the clay, puts it away, and moves on.

entries.description: Three people in yellow Rebuilder coats haul a large pelican case to the camera. They set up a folding table. The leader keys the intercom: 'Collective medical sweep. We have iodine supplements and a functioning marrow density scanner. We just need to screen your population for the geographic radiation map.'

choices.text: Cycle them into the medical bay. Let them test everyone.
choices.outcomeDescription: They find early-stage marrow degradation in three children. The iodine pills they leave behind buy you exactly six months.

choices.text: Cycle survivors through the airlock one at a time. The medics stay outside.
choices.outcomeDescription: The scanner works slowly in the cold, and two cases are flagged before the battery freezes. They leave the iodine in the slot without complaining.

choices.text: Tell them you have no medical needs. Close the blast shutter.
choices.outcomeDescription: They pack up the pelican case and haul it toward the next valley. Ten days later, one of your mechanics starts shedding hair in clumps.

entries.description: An elderly man in a threadbare pre-war uniform stands at the outer camera. It is negative twenty-two degrees outside, and he is not wearing a respirator. He carries nothing. He looks directly into the lens and says: 'I poured the concrete for the number four structural support. I know where the secondary access tunnel is buried.'

choices.text: Cycle him through the airlock. Give him a chair and a hot ration.
choices.outcomeDescription: He talks for two hours, drawing schematics from memory on the back of an old manifest. The tunnel is real, sealed but functional. He stays, and he earns his calories.

choices.text: Interrogate him through the intercom. The blast door stays shut.
choices.outcomeDescription: He nods slowly. He recites a string of coordinates and a demolition protocol over the speaker. When you check the perimeter later, the tunnel is exactly where he said. The camera shows he walked into the tree line to die.

entries.description: A figure in a snow-caked tactical suit pushes a lead-shielded canister through the transfer slot. They don't speak. There is no manifest. Taped to the lid is a torn scrap of Mylar with handwritten text: 'In case of perimeter compromise.' The canister contains high-grade SSKI iodine solution.

choices.text: Keep the canister. Log it into the medical inventory.
choices.outcomeDescription: The courier leaves. The iodine is clean, manufactured two weeks ago. The paranoia of why it was delivered will last much longer.

choices.text: Push the canister back through the slot. Accept nothing anomalous.
choices.outcomeDescription: The canister drops into the snow. The courier stands still for exactly sixty seconds, picks it up, and walks away.

entries.description: Inspector Nara of the Hydro Barons holds a water-stained ledger to the camera. 'You've exceeded your aquifer draw allowance by four hundred and twenty liters since winter started,' she says. Her breath pluming in the cold. 'The Authority requires a penalty payment of one hundred and eighty liters of purified water, or the valve gets welded shut.'

choices.text: Cycle eighteen standardized water canisters into the airlock.
choices.outcomeDescription: She tests the purity of one canister with a chemical strip, nods, and stamps your ledger page in red ink. The debt is clear. For now.

choices.text: Push two military-grade medkits through the slot. Offer them in trade.
choices.outcomeDescription: She looks at the medkits for a long time. She calculates the extortionate exchange rate in her head, takes them, and marks the account settled.

choices.text: Present the bunker's internal intake telemetry. Dispute the figure.
choices.outcomeDescription: She compares your printouts against her ledger. She frowns, files a formal arbitration dispute form, and leaves without collecting a drop. The problem is just deferred.

entries.description: An older woman in a grey woven coat stands before the blast door. She carries a sealed clay urn. 'I am Elder Cassia,' she says through the intercom. Her voice is calm, devoid of the usual desperation. 'I require access to your exterior foundation anchor to perform a consecration of the earth. In return, the Ash Sign will include this coordinate in our high-altitude barometric warning broadcasts.'

choices.text: Permit the ritual. Unlock the perimeter gate but keep the blast door sealed.
choices.outcomeDescription: She pours black ash from the urn over the concrete anchor, murmuring for twenty minutes. Three weeks later, a coded radio transmission warns you of a massive storm system sixty hours before it hits.

choices.text: Refuse. No cult rituals on the perimeter.
choices.outcomeDescription: She shows no anger. She places a small pebble on top of the camera housing and walks back into the wasteland. You are never included in the broadcast network.

entries.description: A man wrapped in layers of stitched canvas holds an oilcloth tube to the lens. 'Topographical survey. Forty kilometer radius,' he says, coughing heavily between words. 'Marks the hot zones, the sinkholes, and the Garrison kill-boxes. Accurate as of last week. I need calories or medicine. Pick one.'

choices.text: Push five compressed ration bricks into the airlock.
choices.outcomeDescription: He snatches the bricks, bites one immediately, and shoves the tube through the slot. The map is drawn in ballpoint pen on the back of a billboard tarp. It saves two patrol teams from walking into an irradiated sinkhole.

choices.text: Trade two blisters of broad-spectrum antibiotics.
choices.outcomeDescription: He holds the blister packs up to the pale light, verifying the foil seals. He passes the map through. The intel is good, but you've traded critical infection control for it.

choices.text: Decline the trade. The wasteland changes too fast for maps.
choices.outcomeDescription: He coughs violently, caps the oilcloth tube, and turns away. A month later, your expedition truck falls through a collapsed ice-bridge that was probably marked on that tarp.

entries.description: A Garrison corporal shoves a shackled woman into the camera's view. Her yellow Rebuilder coat is torn and stained with diesel. 'Transport broke an axle two klicks north,' the corporal barks over the intercom. 'We need to lock this saboteur in your holding cells for forty-eight hours until the recovery truck gets here. Garrison emergency requisition.'

choices.text: Cycle them into the secure storage room. Let the Garrison lock her up.
choices.outcomeDescription: The corporal sits in the corridor smoking cheap cigarettes for two days. The recovery truck finally arrives, and the woman is hauled away. She never said a word.

choices.text: Refuse the requisition. You are a civilian installation, not a black site.
choices.outcomeDescription: The corporal curses at the camera, keys his radio, and forces the shackled woman to march out into the freezing wind toward the treeline. You do not watch them go.

choices.text: Tell the corporal to put the prisoner on the intercom before you decide.
choices.outcomeDescription: The woman leans into the grille. 'I was diverting hydro-paste to the outer ring civilians. The Garrison caught me.' The corporal pulls her back violently. You refuse them entry. At least you know what you're complicit in.

entries.description: A Rebuilder educator arrives dragging a heavy canvas sled. It is loaded with basic literacy and mathematics workbooks, printed on the reverse sides of old municipal tax forms. 'A mind rots just as fast as a body,' she says, wiping frost from her visor. 'I can stay for five days to teach the children. If you feed me.'

choices.text: Cycle her in. Pay the caloric cost of an extra mouth for five days.
choices.outcomeDescription: The children sit on the cold floor and learn fractions. By the third day, three adults join the back row to learn how to read. It feels almost like before the war.

choices.text: Trade two days of rations for the workbooks through the slot. No entry.
choices.outcomeDescription: She pushes the stacks of paper through the slot. The workbooks go into the common room. The children stare at the tax forms, but someone starts trying to teach them.

entries.description: A man in a perfectly clean grey robe stands in front of the camera. The wind is howling, but he stands entirely still. He taps a dosimeter strapped to his wrist against the lens. It reads 280 mSv. 'Is there room for one more,' he asks over the intercom, 'or should I walk to the next door?'

choices.text: Cycle him in. He's irradiated, but not contagious.
choices.outcomeDescription: He strips the robe in the airlock and accepts a shelter jumpsuit. He never takes off the dosimeter, and he never speaks of the Ash Sign again. He just scrubs the filters and waits.

choices.text: Tell him his dose is over the safety threshold. He cannot enter.
choices.outcomeDescription: He nods once, deeply. He turns his back to the camera and begins walking south down the broken highway. He has nowhere to go.

entries.description: A man hauling a heavy ground-penetrating radar sled stops at your door. He wears the Hydro Baron insignia. 'We have a pressure drop on the primary main,' he shouts. 'It runs eight meters directly below your sublevel. I need to drill a six-inch test bore through your foundation to run a camera down.'

choices.text: Evacuate the sublevel. Let him drill.
choices.outcomeDescription: The drill screams for six hours, vibrating dust from the ceiling. He finds a hairline fracture, patches it with expanding resin, and leaves a spool of copper wire as thanks.

choices.text: Refuse the bore hole. Your foundation integrity is non-negotiable.
choices.outcomeDescription: He does not argue. He packs up his sled and marks his map. A week later you hear muffled subterranean explosions as they collapse that section of the main entirely.

entries.description: A woman in a matte-black parka stands before the camera. She carries no visible weapons, but her posture screams military. 'I have forty-eight hours of decrypted Garrison radio chatter on a flash drive,' she says. 'I want seven days of raw low-frequency signal logs from your antenna array. Straight trade. No questions.'

choices.text: Copy the antenna logs to a drive. Make the trade.
choices.outcomeDescription: She takes your drive, leaves hers, and vanishes. The Garrison intercepts reveal three supply movements you can intercept. But you've given away your shelter's exact communication fingerprint.

choices.text: Refuse the trade. Signal logs are a security risk.
choices.outcomeDescription: She nods once, tapping her earpiece. 'Acknowledged. Civilian asset uncooperative.' She walks away into the whiteout.

entries.description: A woman in Garrison armor stands at the outer door. She is alone. The rank insignia on her collar has been violently torn off, leaving frayed threads. 'I was ordered to glass a civilian cistern in sector four,' she tells the camera. 'I shot my CO instead. I need to disappear.'

choices.text: Cycle her in. Disarm her in the airlock.
choices.outcomeDescription: She drops her sidearm and tactical vest in the transfer tray. She knows every Garrison patrol route and every blind spot. Her tactical knowledge saves your scavengers twice in the first week.

choices.text: Tell her she's too hot. You can't risk Garrison retaliation.
choices.outcomeDescription: She doesn't argue. She pulls the torn fabric on her collar tight against the cold, turns her back, and walks steadily into the storm.

choices.text: Tell her to wait. Broadcast her coordinates to the Garrison command net.
choices.outcomeDescription: A heavy transport arrives in less than an hour. The camera catches the muzzle flash of her execution in the snow. Your people watch the feed in dead silence.

entries.description: A Rebuilder tech hauls an aluminum transmitter box up to the camera. 'Passive relay node,' he says, tapping the aluminum casing. 'I need to bolt it to your antenna mast. It bridges our northern network. You get access to our unencrypted weather telemetry. We get a stronger signal bounce. Win-win.'

choices.text: Open the perimeter gate. Let him climb the mast.
choices.outcomeDescription: He splices the node into your array in under an hour. That evening, your radio starts pulling down localized barometric pressure readings and clean-water exchange rates.

choices.text: Refuse. The node makes the bunker a triangulated point on their grid.
choices.outcomeDescription: He shrugs, picks up the aluminum box, and hauls it back toward the highway. The bunker stays off the grid. And blind to the weather.

entries.description: A scavenger kneels in front of the lens. She unpacks a soldering iron and a voltage meter from a rusted toolbox. 'I can clean the oxide off your battery contacts,' she says, 'and recalibrate your rad-badges. Two days of heat and six meals.'

choices.text: Cycle her into the workshop area. Pay the six rations.
choices.outcomeDescription: She strips the dosimeters down to the circuitry. They haven't worked this well since the bombs dropped. She sleeps curled under the workbench.

choices.text: Negotiate down to just the dosimeters. Three rations. No overnight stay.
choices.outcomeDescription: She works in the airlock with a headlamp. The badges read cleanly, but her hands shake from the cold the entire time.

entries.description: Three Garrison soldiers stand at the door. Two carry rifles at the low ready. The third holds a clipboard. 'Emergency Civilian Armaments Ordinance,' the inspector announces. 'Open the door. We are here to inventory all small arms. Refusal is punishable under martial law.'

choices.text: Open the blast door. Surrender the armory keys for inspection.
choices.outcomeDescription: They log every serial number and weigh your ammunition stocks. The inspector signs a carbon-copy form and hands it to you. 'Compliant.' They leave without taking anything.

choices.text: Refuse entry. Cite civilian charter sovereignty.
choices.outcomeDescription: The inspector stares at the camera for a long moment. 'Noted.' He checks a box on his clipboard. They do not force the door, but you are now on a list.

choices.text: Allow them in, but stall them while the heavy weapons are hidden in the ventilation shafts.
choices.outcomeDescription: The inspector notes the missing serial numbers from the old inventory logs but accepts your lie about mechanical failure. It buys you time, nothing more.

entries.description: A man in a thick rubberized coat leaves a bright crimson smear across the camera lens as he drags himself to the door. 'High pressure line blew,' he gasps over the intercom, clutching a massive laceration on his left forearm. Blood is pooling fast on the concrete step. 'Baron's pumping station is six hours. I'll bleed out in one.'

choices.text: Cycle him into the airlock. Burn a medical kit to suture and clamp the artery.
choices.outcomeDescription: You get a tourniquet on him just in time. He sleeps on the floor for twenty-four hours, then limps away. Three days later, a crate of purification tablets is left at your door with a Baron's wax seal.

choices.text: Push a tight pressure dressing through the slot. No entry.
choices.outcomeDescription: He wraps the dressing himself with shaking, bloody hands. He makes it over the ridge line. You don't know if he made it any further.

choices.text: Leave the door sealed. Medical supplies are strictly for residents.
choices.outcomeDescription: He stops banging on the door after twenty minutes. The cold takes him before the blood loss does. A Baron patrol recovers his frozen body two days later.

entries.description: Three Ash Sign zealots in heavy robes block the camera lens. The leader carries a bucket of thick, grey slurry. 'Your air intakes are breathing corrupted wind,' he chants into the intercom. 'We must pour the holy ash into your filtration system to bind the unseen death. It is required.'

choices.text: Tell them to step away from the intake vents or be fired upon.
choices.outcomeDescription: They step back. The leader smears a thick red cross on the blast door with the slurry. Your engineers breathe a sigh of relief.

choices.text: Offer a compromise: they can burn the ash in a brazier outside the intake, but nothing goes inside.
choices.outcomeDescription: They argue among themselves before agreeing. They burn the slurry in a rusted barrel. The smoke gets sucked into your filters, clogging them by 15%, but the zealots leave satisfied.

entries.description: The radio receiver crackles to life at exactly 03:00. The signal is weak, bouncing off the ionosphere. A woman's voice cuts through the static. 'This is MERIDIAN. Coastal relay. I have three hundred hours of archived survivor testimony. Is anyone listening in Sector Four?'

choices.text: Key the mic. Send a brief acknowledgment burst.
choices.outcomeDescription: A long pause follows on the static. Then: 'Acknowledged, Sector Four. Broadcasting at 06:00 local. I do not have much time.' It gives people hope.

choices.text: Maintain radio silence. Don't reveal your active receiver status.
choices.outcomeDescription: The voice loops the request three times into the dead air, then cuts out. You never hear from MERIDIAN again.

entries.description: A woman leans heavily against the outer blast door, panting so hard her breath fogs the lens entirely. She hauls a reinforced Pelican case up to the camera. 'Potassium iodide and anti-nausea,' she gasps. 'Expired three years ago, but the blister packs are intact. I need food.'

choices.text: Trade four days of rations for the expired meds.
choices.outcomeDescription: She takes the food and leaves the case in the airlock. Your medic tests a tablet. 'Efficacy is down to maybe sixty percent,' he notes. It's better than nothing.

choices.text: Refuse the trade. Expired meds aren't worth the calories.
choices.outcomeDescription: She swears, picks up the heavy case, and stumbles back toward the frozen highway. You just hope your thyroids hold out.

entries.description: A Garrison transport idles in the snow. A corporal kicks seven civilians out of the back of the truck. 'Non-compliance with the Allocation Act,' he barks into the intercom. 'They're off our ledger. You want 'em, they're yours.' The truck grinds into gear and leaves them shivering in the ash.

choices.text: Cycle all seven through the airlock. Adjust the ledger.
choices.outcomeDescription: They stumble in, half-frozen and terrified. Your water reserves drop sharply on the spreadsheet. The Garrison has offloaded their dead weight onto you.

choices.text: Admit three—only the able-bodied.
choices.outcomeDescription: You make the selection over the intercom. The three walk in. The four left outside don't even scream. They just huddle together on the concrete step.

choices.text: Keep the door sealed. Seven mouths will break your supply math.
choices.outcomeDescription: They stand by the door for two hours. One of them is a child. When the sun starts to set, they finally walk north. They won't make it to the next shelter.

entries.description: A Rebuilder driver hammers on the blast door with a socket wrench. 'Snapped a drive shaft two hundred meters out,' he yells. The wind threatens to drown him out. 'We're hauling antibiotics for three downstream bunkers. I need a warm bay and two heavy mechanics, or those shelters lose a lot of people to sepsis this week.'

choices.text: Open the vehicle bay. Put your mechanics on the line.
choices.outcomeDescription: It takes four hours of swearing and acetylene torches, but the truck rolls out under its own power. The driver leaves a flat of anti-nausea medication on a workbench before driving into the whiteout.

choices.text: Push a heavy tool chest through the airlock. Do not risk your own people.
choices.outcomeDescription: They haul the chest through the snow. It takes them eight hours to do the repair in the freezing wind. They return the tools coated in ice and blood.

choices.text: Keep the door sealed. Your tools and personnel stay inside.
choices.outcomeDescription: The driver curses your bunker over an open radio frequency. They wait fourteen hours for a tow rig. The downstream shelters suffer for it.

entries.description: A girl no older than sixteen is dragging herself through the ash drifts. Her left leg is shattered below the knee. The blood trail stretches back out of sight into the fog. She has no faction patches and no gear, just a deep scalp wound and a refusal to die quietly.

choices.text: Cycle her into the med-bay. Burn a medkit to set the bone.
choices.outcomeDescription: She screams when the bone is set, then sleeps for two days. Her name is Rin. Once she can walk with a crutch, she starts repairing your ruptured air hoses without being asked.

choices.text: Splint the leg in the airlock and radio for a Rebuilder med-sled.
choices.outcomeDescription: You push her back out into the snow to wait for the sled. Three weeks later, a courier drops two blister packs of antibiotics at your door. There is no note.

entries.description: A woman in a salt-crusted maritime immersion suit stands in the thaw mud outside the blast door. She carries an encrypted naval transponder. 'Northern Convoy icebreaker extraction is Day 360,' she states over the comms. 'I need your occupant manifest and fifteen liters of purified coolant water to secure your berths.'

choices.text: Transmit the manifest. Cycle three canisters of clean water into the airlock.
choices.outcomeDescription: She logs the names into a hardened datapad and pushes a VHF rendezvous beacon through the transfer slot. You have a way out.

choices.text: Log the extraction coordinates. Broadcast them unencrypted on all frequencies.
choices.outcomeDescription: The woman curses as the transmission goes live. Across the sector, dead radios suddenly ping with desperate acknowledgments. You just started a stampede.

choices.text: Refuse the berths. You aren't abandoning the sector now.
choices.outcomeDescription: She stares at the camera for a long time. Then she salutes the lens and begins the long, agonizing walk back toward the frozen coastline.

entries.description: A man smelling strongly of sulfur and forge-scale pushes a heavy iron wheelbarrow up to the camera. It is full of spent 152mm artillery casings. 'High Granite Arsenal,' he wheezes. 'I need six ration packs for the forge crews. You can melt the brass down for whatever you want.'

choices.text: Trade six ration packs for the raw brass.
choices.outcomeDescription: He tips the wheelbarrow over, sending the heavy brass cylinders clattering onto the concrete step. He takes the tins, nods once, and leaves the cart behind.

choices.text: Refuse the trade. Brass has no caloric value.
choices.outcomeDescription: He spits onto the frozen concrete, grips the heavy iron handles of his wheelbarrow, and continues pushing his useless metal down the road.

entries.description: Three rail workers in grease-soaked wool coats stand on the surface tracks beside an armored steam handcar. 'Garrison Checkpoint Gamma is two miles up,' the foreman says over the wire. 'Hide the handcar in your outer bay overnight. We'll wire your telegraph link for free.'

choices.text: Open the outer blast doors. Let them push the handcar inside.
choices.outcomeDescription: They sleep under the boiler of their handcar. By dawn, they are gone, leaving a fully repaired telegraph link and three spools of copper wire.

choices.text: Tell them no. Then radio their coordinates to Checkpoint Gamma for the flour bounty.
choices.outcomeDescription: A Garrison half-track intercepts them at the rail switch an hour later. You get your flour. The railway union marks your bunker with a black triangle.

entries.description: Four penal sappers in mud-caked rags and burlap foot-wraps beat on the blast door with an iron pry-bar. Their skin is peeling in sheets from severe radiation exposure. 'We need Prussian blue and iodine!' one screams into the camera. 'The Garrison marched us through a hot zone to clear rubble! Help us!'

choices.text: Cycle them into the quarantine cellar. Administer Prussian blue.
choices.outcomeDescription: They vomit for three days straight, but the chelating agents work. They leave an unexploded demolition charge as payment and promise to come back to dig your drainage trenches when the thaw hits.

choices.text: Fire a burst through the gunport into the snow at their feet.
choices.outcomeDescription: They flinch at the gunfire, then stand there for a long moment, staring at the camera. Eventually, they turn and limp back out into the freezing mud to die.

entries.description: Two orderlies in white linen coats pull a heavy sledge up to the blast door. Three people lie on it, stumps wrapped in blood-soaked bandages. 'Salt hospital is another four miles,' the lead orderly gasps over the comms. 'We just need two hours in your exhaust vents so they don't freeze to death, and some boiled water.'

choices.text: Cycle two canisters of clean, boiling water out to them. Reroute exhaust heat to the vestibule.
choices.outcomeDescription: They huddle around the vents, drinking the boiling water like it's a religious sacrament. When they leave, they drop a sealed box of surgical scalpel blades in the airlock.

choices.text: Keep the hatch locked. Rerouting exhaust compromises interior thermal efficiency.
choices.outcomeDescription: The orderlies don't have the energy to argue. They grab the tow ropes and drag the sledge back into the freezing fog.

entries.description: An armored half-track idles outside in the blizzard, its diesel engine knocking violently. Captain Alder hammers on the intercom panel. 'I need a can of glycol antifreeze!' he yells over the wind. 'It's minus thirty-eight. If my radiator cracks, my crew freezes in their seats before dawn.'

choices.text: Cycle one canister of industrial glycol through the airlock.
choices.outcomeDescription: Alder pours the viscous blue fluid straight into the hissing expansion tank. He leaves a crated lead-acid battery in the airlock before the half-track grinds away into the snow.

choices.text: Refuse. The bunker needs every drop of antifreeze for its own heating loop.
choices.outcomeDescription: Alder kicks the blast door, screaming something lost to the wind. The half-track stalls an hour later. You monitor their dying radio calls until the battery dies.

entries.description: Commander Talia skis up to the blast doors, her snow-camo painted with rust streaks. 'Garrison armor is probing the lower road,' she tells the camera. 'If your optical sensors spot their half-tracks, ping the coordinates to this frequency. I have smoked turnips for your cooperation.'

choices.text: Accept the terms. Feed Garrison convoy data to the militia.
choices.outcomeDescription: She drops a burlap sack of root vegetables in the snow and skis away. For the next three weeks, you watch Garrison trucks burn from a safe distance.

choices.text: Refuse. Active espionage violates your neutrality protocol.
choices.outcomeDescription: She doesn't argue. She adjusts her goggles and kicks off into the whiteout. The war remains theirs to fight.

entries.description: Four men smelling heavily of burnt grain and pulverized concrete haul blackened canvas sacks to the door. 'Garrison dropped artillery on the mill,' the lead man wheezes. 'We salvaged fifty kilos of flour. We need a roll of silicone hatch gasket to seal what's left of the cellar, or the radiation will take us.'

choices.text: Trade one silicone hatch gasket for the fifty kilos of flour.
choices.outcomeDescription: The gasket goes out, the heavy sacks come in. The flour tastes faintly of cordite and ash, but it bakes into dense, calorie-heavy bread.

choices.text: Refuse. Smoke-tainted grain from a shelled silo is an ingestion hazard.
choices.outcomeDescription: They shoulder the heavy canvas sacks in silence. You watch them trudge away, carrying the only thing of value they have left.

entries.description: An Ash Sign ascetic stands barefoot in the toxic slush, clutching a lead-lined wicker basket. He holds up a chunk of smooth, green vitrified glass from a detonation crater. 'The fire that cleansed the world left us a piece of its heart,' he murmurs. The external dosimeter spikes hard to 150 µSv/h.

choices.text: Open the transfer slot. Confiscate the glass and drop it directly into a lead storage pig.
choices.outcomeDescription: You seal the highly radioactive slag in the lead pig. The ascetic howls in protest and batters the steel door with his fists until his hands bleed, then finally wanders away.

choices.text: Cut the intercom and drop the blast shutters. The radiation hazard is too high.
choices.outcomeDescription: He leaves the glowing green slag on the concrete step. You have to send someone out in a heavy suit the next morning to shovel it into a disposal drum.

entries.description: Three people huddle by the blast door, their skin mottled with heavy yellow blisters. Their eyelids are swollen shut. 'Old munitions dump in the thaw mud,' one gasps, clawing blindly at his neck. 'Sulfur mustard. We need clean water for our eyes before the blisters burst.'

choices.text: Cycle three canisters of clean water into the airlock with a saline drip kit.
choices.outcomeDescription: They flush their eyes in the freezing air, screaming as the water hits the chemical burns. They leave an antique mercury barometer on the step before staggering blindly south.

choices.text: Seal the blast door. Chemical off-gassing will contaminate the air scrubbers.
choices.outcomeDescription: They scratch blindly at the steel door until their fingernails tear, begging for water. Eventually, the cold finishes what the mustard gas started.

entries.description: Camera 3 catches a figure in a white winter smock splicing into your exterior telegraph trunk line. When you hit the siren, he doesn't run. He holds up an STD-9 credential and speaks into a hand-held mic. 'I need two battery cells. I'll trade an unencrypted one-time cipher pad for Garrison secure frequencies.'

choices.text: Trade two charged batteries for the cipher pad.
choices.outcomeDescription: He leaves the book of randomized codes wrapped in oilcloth, takes the batteries, and disappears. You now have ears on the Garrison.

choices.text: Trip the internal breaker. Sever the external trunk line to break the tap.
choices.outcomeDescription: The comms board goes dark. The operative shrugs, packs his splicing kit, and walks away. You are deaf to the outside world for the next week.

entries.description: A man in a canvas drysuit and heavy brass diving helmet slogs out of the flooded aqueduct. Water freezes instantly on his suit. 'Main pump manifold is frozen,' he radios. 'I need two liters of high-proof alcohol to melt the valve seals. We do this, you get water pressure back.'

choices.text: Trade two bottles of grain alcohol through the airlock.
choices.outcomeDescription: He wades back into the freezing black water. Four hours later, your sink taps cough dust, then sputter, then run with a steady stream of cold, clear water.

choices.text: Refuse. High-proof alcohol is reserved for surgical sterilization.
choices.outcomeDescription: He doesn't argue. He turns around, his heavy brass helmet catching the weak sunlight, and submerges. The pipes stay dry.

entries.description: Two Garrison spotters in snow camouflage are lying prone on your bunker's concrete exhaust mound, scanning the valley with heavy optics. One keys the intercom. 'Our TRC-119 battery is dead. Run a 12-volt charging cable up the airshaft, or we can't call in the fire mission on the militia camp.'

choices.text: Run the jumper cables up the shaft. Provide the power.
choices.outcomeDescription: They charge the battery for an hour. Fifteen minutes after they leave, you hear the rolling thunder of 120mm mortar fire down in the valley. They leave a rusted tin of 7.62mm ammunition behind.

choices.text: Refuse the charge. The bunker is strictly non-combatant.
choices.outcomeDescription: The spotter curses into the dead handset. They pack up their optics and march back toward Checkpoint Gamma, marking your bunker's grid coordinates in a red ledger.

entries.description: A man entirely coated in white salt dust sets a wooden crate down heavily. It's packed with Comp-B demolition charges. 'We hit a granite shelf at four hundred meters,' he says, voice deadened by the dust. 'I'll give you two blocks of high explosive for one sack of ammonium nitrate fertilizer. Our hydroponics beds are dying.'

choices.text: Trade one sack of ammonium nitrate fertilizer for the explosives.
choices.outcomeDescription: He takes the heavy fertilizer sack and slides two blocks of yellowed Comp-B into the airlock. You carefully store the high explosives far away from the reactor.

choices.text: Refuse. High explosives are too dangerous to store inside a sealed bunker.
choices.outcomeDescription: He doesn't show any emotion through the layer of salt on his face. He picks up the heavy crate and begins the long walk back to the hoists.

entries.description: Sixteen people huddle by the blast door, shivering violently. Their clothes reek of smoke. 'Kiln collapsed in the permafrost,' a woman calls out. 'We have fifty dry peat fuel bricks. Let us sleep on your garage floor for the night, or the kids won't wake up tomorrow.'

choices.text: Cycle them into the vehicle bay. Take the peat fuel.
choices.outcomeDescription: They pile into the garage, filling it with the smell of woodsmoke and unwashed bodies. They leave fifty dense blocks of peat near the furnace. They are gone by first light.

choices.text: Refuse entry. Sixteen extra lungs will crash the air scrubber.
choices.outcomeDescription: You cut the external microphone so you don't have to listen to them beg. In the morning, you find a few of the children frozen to the concrete step. The adults are gone.

entries.description: Two sailors in heavy maritime parkas pull up on an armored airboat. They carry naval submachine guns. 'Aurora Borealis scout team,' the officer calls over the intercom. 'We are verifying manifests. Present a calibrated radon detector and viable seed stock, or you are struck from the evacuation list.'

choices.text: Push the radon monitor and the Strain-7 rye seeds through the transfer slot.
choices.outcomeDescription: The officer checks the dosimeter calibration and inspects the rhizomes. He stamps your manifest with a heavy steel die. 'Be at the coast on Day 360.' Your ticket is punched.

choices.text: Admit you do not have the required scientific salvage.
choices.outcomeDescription: The officer doesn't even blink. He draws a heavy red line through your bunker's designation on his clipboard. 'Dead weight stays,' he says, and the airboat throttles away.

entries.description: Dr. Chen is hammering on the blast door with a wrench. A snowmobile driver is slumped against the concrete next to her, both legs blackened and rigid to the knee. 'I need your airlock, a surgical bone chisel, and three gallons of boiling water!' she screams. 'We take them now or the sepsis hits his heart!'

choices.text: Cycle them into the airlock. Provide the bone chisel and boiling water.
choices.outcomeDescription: The screaming echoes through the bunker vents for an hour. When it's over, Dr. Chen drags the severed legs back out into the snow to freeze. The driver lives, and he's yours now.

choices.text: Refuse entry. An amputation in the airlock is a massive biohazard.
choices.outcomeDescription: Chen screams at the camera until her voice goes hoarse. The driver dies of septic shock just before midnight. Chen leaves the body on your step.

entries.description: An engineer with a dial-gauge micrometer spends an hour taking readings off the exterior collar of your air intake. He finally keys the intercom. 'Permafrost is thawing. You have a ten-millimeter deflection in your primary foundation block. It's going to shear unless you brace it with a steel culvert jack.'

choices.text: Trade a high-tensile steel brace and two rations. Let him reinforce the foundation.
choices.outcomeDescription: He spends six hours welding the brace into the bedrock fissures. The micro-tremors in the floor stop completely, and the radon readings drop to zero.

choices.text: Ignore the warning. Your bunker's poured concrete can withstand the thaw.
choices.outcomeDescription: He shakes his head and walks away. Three days later, a sound like a cannon shot echoes through the sublevels. A jagged fissure tears across the floor of the generator room.

entries.description: A man wearing lead-lined x-ray aprons drags an iron sledge that melts a steaming trench through the snow. 'Strontium-90 RTG!' he screams, his face blistered and peeling from acute radiation exposure. 'A hundred and twenty watts of permanent heat! I need five medical rations or I'm dead by morning!'

choices.text: Trade the medical rations. Secure the RTG in a shielded transport cask.
choices.outcomeDescription: You load the glowing core into the lead cask and push the meds out. He takes them with shaking hands. The core is integrated into your heating loop, providing permanent, silent warmth.

choices.text: Fire warning shots. The ambient radiation off that sledge is a death sentence.
choices.outcomeDescription: He doesn't have the strength to argue. He turns the heavy iron sledge around and drags his prize back into the fog. You doubt he made it another mile.

entries.description: Two men wearing climbing spurs and leather lineman belts are inspecting your external junction box. 'Testing line continuity to the Arsenal,' the foreman yells over the wind. 'Your box is the only active relay in ten miles. Give us an hour and some solder, and we'll patch you into the guild network.'

choices.text: Push a spool of rosin-core solder through the slot. Grant access.
choices.outcomeDescription: They work for an hour, their breath freezing in the air. When they finish, your telegraph chatters to life with traffic from the Arsenal and the coastal stations.

choices.text: Refuse access. Splicing external lines compromises internal communications security.
choices.outcomeDescription: The foreman spits, kicks the frozen dirt away from the junction box, and leads his partner back down the dead tracks.

entries.description: On the 360th morning, the camera feed shows a crowd of people standing in pale, unfiltered sunlight. Agronomists, rail switchmen, salt miners, and a few Garrison defectors. 'We're breaking ground on the new settlement down in the valley,' a woman says over the intercom. 'We're asking everyone left alive to open their doors.'

choices.text: Throw the dog-bolts. Open the blast door. Let the sunlight in.
choices.outcomeDescription: The steel door groans on hinges that haven't moved in a year. The air outside is cold, but the sky is clear. The year of ash is over.

choices.text: Keep the bunker sealed. The atmospheric scrubbers indicate trace isotopes remain.
choices.outcomeDescription: They wait for twenty minutes. When the door doesn't move, they nod, turn around, and walk down into the valley to rebuild the world without you.

entries.description: A man in an oiled canvas duster stops at your door. He sets down a heavy wooden case, opening it to reveal dozens of magnetic recording reels. 'Pre-war telemetry from the Spine bunkers,' he says. 'Five liters of water for a spool. Learn how the world ended.'

choices.text: Trade five liters of water for the telemetry tapes.
choices.outcomeDescription: He takes the jerrycan of water and passes two heavy spool canisters through the airlock. They are stamped with red Department of the Interior seals.

choices.text: Refuse the trade. You don't need ghosts from before the fire.
choices.outcomeDescription: He latches the wooden case shut with a dull snap and walks back out into the freezing fog.

entries.description: A technician wearing heavy insulated gauntlets kicks the snow away from your external conduit array. 'Tempest Network,' he calls out, pointing to a patch on his coat. 'Carrier wave is fluctuating. Need to clamp a meter to your grounding rod to balance the 120Hz circuit.'

choices.text: Remotely unlock the exterior terminal cover. Supply him with two copper ground clips.
choices.outcomeDescription: He works for ten minutes, his heavy pliers snapping in the cold. When he locks the panel back up, the persistent AC hum on your shortwave radio vanishes entirely.

choices.text: Keep the terminal locked. Network engineers are just spies with tools.
choices.outcomeDescription: He doesn't argue. He makes a mark on a laminated clipboard with a grease pencil and walks toward the next relay tower.

entries.description: A woman carrying a thick leather folio knocks three times on the steel door. 'Tempest Network,' she says, uncapping a fountain pen. 'Conducting a census for the regional authority. I need a full headcount of living adults, minors, and recent casualties.'

choices.text: Read the bunker roster over the intercom. Slide a signed verification slip through the slot.
choices.outcomeDescription: She records each name meticulously in archival ink. 'Your existence is formally registered,' she says, sliding a stamped receipt back through the slot.

choices.text: Refuse to disclose the roster. Information is a liability.
choices.outcomeDescription: She marks a heavy black 'X' in the ledger under your coordinates. 'Uncooperative,' she murmurs to herself, snapping the folio shut.

entries.description: A man sets up a cracked parabolic microphone near the bunker exhaust manifold. 'I need to record your diesel plant's acoustic signature,' he says into his lapel mic. 'I'm building a baseline archive of the valley's mechanical harmonics. Need it to run for two minutes.'

choices.text: Burn the fuel. Let him record the generator.
choices.outcomeDescription: You crank the diesels. He watches the needle on his Nagra reel-to-reel bounce for two minutes, gives a thumbs up, and slides a pristine speaker cone through the transfer box before leaving.

choices.text: Cut the intercom. You don't have fuel to waste on acoustic archiving.
choices.outcomeDescription: He waits in the freezing silence for five minutes, carefully collapses his tripod, and walks away across the snow.

entries.description: A woman carrying a wooden shoulder yoke heavily laden with canvas sacks stops by the blast door. 'Unrefined brine salt from the dry lakebed,' she calls out. 'I'll trade ten kilos for two ampoules of medical iodine. The goiter is spreading in the camps.'

choices.text: Trade the iodine. Take the curing salt.
choices.outcomeDescription: She slides the glass ampoules into a padded leather pouch and heaves the heavy, coarse salt sacks into the transfer box. Your meat curing reserves are restocked.

choices.text: Refuse the trade. Medical iodine is strictly rationed.
choices.outcomeDescription: She doesn't argue. She adjusts the heavy wooden yoke across her shoulders and begins the long walk back to the lakebed.

entries.description: A man in a frayed hazmat suit is assembling a steel auger core sampler on the dirt mound covering your intake vents. 'Taking a fifty-centimeter topsoil core,' he calls toward the camera. 'Plotting cesium-137 decay for the Reconstruction Authority. Don't shoot.'

choices.text: Lower your weapon. Let him take the soil core.
choices.outcomeDescription: He grunts as he twists the auger into the frozen earth. He bottles the dirt in a lead-lined tube, slips a hand-drawn topographical radiation map under the door in thanks, and leaves.

choices.text: Cycle a round into the chamber. Order him off the berm.
choices.outcomeDescription: The crack of the rifle bolt echoing through the external speaker is enough. He throws his hands up, disassembles the auger, and hurries away.

entries.description: A man in a burlap hood stands rigidly in front of the door. He holds up a clear plastic cassette tape. 'The Great Silence,' he whispers, his voice barely carrying over the wind. 'The last broadcast before the sky burned. Give me a tin of animal fat, and the truth is yours.'

choices.text: Trade a tin of rendered lard for the cassette.
choices.outcomeDescription: He takes the lard and leaves the tape in the airlock. When you play it, it's just twenty minutes of static, followed by the faint sound of weeping.

choices.text: Refuse the trade. Do not engage with the cult.
choices.outcomeDescription: He stares at the camera lens for a long time, then takes a handful of grey ash from a pouch and scatters it over your intake vent before walking away.

entries.description: An old man wearing dual jeweler's loupes over thick spectacles stands at the door, leaning on a white cane. He's entirely blind. 'Your master clock is thirteen seconds fast,' he says, tapping his cane on the concrete. 'I can hear the escapement through the wall. Let me wire a pulse relay to your telegraph line. We are synchronizing the valley.'

choices.text: Allow him to install the relay. Synchronize your clocks with the Tempest network.
choices.outcomeDescription: He works entirely by touch, wiring a small magnetic coil to the clock's pendulum. The shelter now ticks in flawless, eerie lockstep with every other clock in the valley.

choices.text: Refuse the relay. You keep your own time.
choices.outcomeDescription: The old man frowns, taps his cane twice against the bulkhead, and shuffles away into the snow.
